reuse.why: Extends the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend and adds a shared isNonWorkingDay, but getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange re-derive the daily-skip-vs-move decision instead of calling one shared per-occurrence adjustment.

duplication.why: The 'daily + skipWeekend ? skip non-working day : move via getDateWithSkippedWeekend' dispatch is written three times (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange), and bounded-search loops are repeated in firstWeekdayOccurrence and getUpcomingDates.

placement.why: Holiday/weekend logic sits correctly in shared/schedules.ts, but the occurrence-adjustment rule for the new range handler and upcoming dates lives inline in server/schedules/app.ts rather than in the shared schedule module.

scope.why: Changes are confined to schedule date logic, the new handler, types, tests and release notes; the schedule-template closure refactor is small and related.

maintainability.why: A future change to the weekend/holiday rule must be applied in three diverging copies, getNextDate gains a daily special case that silently ignores noSkipWeekend, and search bounds are ad-hoc magic numbers.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange decide skip-vs-move themselves instead of going through the shared getNextDate/getDateWithSkippedWeekend path; getNextDate's daily branch bypasses its own noSkipWeekend option

disguised_duplication.where: The skip-or-move dispatch appears as a nested if/continue in getUpcomingDates, a differently nested skipWeekend/skipsWeekends block in getDatesInRange, and as firstWeekdayOccurrence in getNextDate; the bounded occurrence scan is reshaped as a 'remaining' counter vs MAX_WEEKDAY_SEARCH

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains a daily-frequency special branch; getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange in server/schedules/app.ts re-implement the daily-skip decision instead of sharing one helper
